feedback: Written before this candidate races, so no outcome is stated for it. Evidence: iteration 7 (5 sensors, 0.04 m spacing, y 0.05 m, mass 0.5 kg) scored 315.27, with oval finish 75%, s-bend progress 0.140 and slalom progress 0.186, and max_error about 0.062 to 0.064 on both bend tracks. Iteration 8 (y 0.03 m) fell to 209.2, so the sensor lead should stay at 0.05 m. Iteration 6 (mass 0.6 kg) gave s-bend 0.181 and slalom 0.191, but the oval finish was 65%. Line loss is now near zero on all tracks, so the remaining bend limit is not sensing coverage. If the 7-sensor array keeps line loss at zero but s-bend and slalom max_error stays near 0.062 with progress below 0.2, the limit is turn response, and wheel_track is the next geometry lever. If the oval finish falls below 65% or oval steering_oscillation rises above 0.25, the denser array is adding noise, so return to five sensors at the iteration-7 spacing.
requested_changes: If s-bend and slalom max_error stays near 0.062 with progress below 0.2 and line loss stays near zero, keep the 7-sensor array and set wheel_track to 0.11 m with mass 0.5 kg. Evidence: iteration 3 at track 0.12 gave s-bend progress 0.177, while narrowing to 0.09 m lowered oval finish to 35% in iteration 5, so only a small step is safe.

If the oval finish falls below 65% with the 7-sensor array, revert to the five-sensor iteration-7 layout (x = -0.08, -0.04, 0, 0.04, 0.08 at y 0.05 m). Evidence: iteration 7 gave 75% oval finish at this layout, while iteration 8 cut it to 40% when the lead changed.

If the 7-sensor array raises line_loss_events or rms_error, try sensor_size 0.012 at the same 0.0267 m spacing, where the gap between footprints is 15 mm and is bridged by the 25 mm tape. Evidence: iteration 1 and 2 used 0.012 m footprints with rms_error 0.019 to 0.024, but the 0.04 m spacing with 0.012 m footprints left a 28 mm gap, which is wider than the tape.
